claims.text: The baseline alloy is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The modified FeNiCrMn alloy is obtained by eliminating Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The as-cast FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
Removing Co can allow the resulting alloy to retain a favorable strength–ductility balance.
Removing Co reduces or otherwise alters the stacking-fault energy of FeNiCrMn relative to CoCrFeMnNi.
Removing Co alters solute–dislocation interactions.
The Co-induced changes in stacking-fault energy and solute–dislocation interactions shift deformation from predominantly dislocation glide toward combined glide and twinning.
High strain rates dynamically activate more deformation twins in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Moderate-to-elevated temperatures promote the proposed dynamic twin activation.
Deformation twins accommodate plastic strain and thereby help maintain ductility.
Deformation twins act as barriers to dislocation motion, increasing work hardening and strength.
At high strain rate and elevated temperature, FeNiCrMn will have a higher twin density than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
At high strain rate and elevated temperature, FeNiCrMn will have a higher strain-hardening rate than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The increased twinning and strain hardening will preserve or improve the strength–ductility balance despite dynamic softening.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi has established dislocation-mediated and twin-mediated deformation behavior.
The proposed mechanism applies between approximately 293 and 773 K and strain rates of approximately 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1.
The dominant deformation mechanism may differ under cryogenic or ultra-high-temperature conditions outside the specified regime.
Testing in an inert atmosphere avoids oxidation sufficiently to isolate dynamic deformation effects.
The magnitude of the changes in twin density and work-hardening rate is unknown and requires experimental calibration.
Failure to observe a statistically significant increase in either twin density or work-hardening rate in FeNiCrMn relative to CoCrFeMnNi under matched dynamic conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
